checkIns.result: Found and fixed a REAL correctness bug this cycle. healthcheck:legacy was GREEN (A/B/C/D as expected) but C_record's own resolved count caught my eye: 30 (23:51 UTC cycle) -> 26 (00:07 UTC cycle) within ~16 minutes with zero market activity in between (Friday evening, RTH long closed). Root-caused to fetchNighthawkOutcomeAnalytics/fetchNighthawkFunnelStats (src/lib/db.ts) windowing their edition_for cutoff off bare Postgres CURRENT_DATE, which resolves in the DB session's UTC timezone -- edition_for is an ET trading-day date, so between ~8pm and midnight ET (exactly the window we're in), CURRENT_DATE has already ticked to the next UTC day and the 14-day window's cutoff lands a day later than intended, prematurely dropping the oldest ET trading day. db.ts already has the identical fix pattern elsewhere (flow-alerts DTE query, '(NOW() AT TIME ZONE America/New_York)::date', with a comment explicitly calling out this exact 8pm-midnight ET failure mode) -- it just was never applied to these two Night Hawk functions. Fixed all 3 call sites (1 in fetchNighthawkOutcomeAnalytics, 2 in fetchNighthawkFunnelStats), added 2 new source-inspection regression tests in db.test.ts (DB integration testing unavailable in this sandbox) proving RED against the pre-fix CURRENT_DATE clauses then GREEN after, tsc --noEmit clean, full local suite kicked off in background (large suite, still running at PR-open time). Opened PR #4816 as draft, subscribed to its activity, staged finding docs/audit/findings-staging/2026-09-12-nighthawk-record-window-utc-anchor.md, added a MARKET-OPEN-VALIDATION.md watch-list entry. This is a real member-visible correctness bug: win_rate_pct/resolved/segments on /record silently shift with zero underlying data change for several hours every trading evening. Impact scope confirmed Legacy-only (fetchNighthawkOutcomeAnalytics/fetchNighthawkFunnelStats have no other callers; 0DTE/Swings use separate tables).

checkIns.note: Real design/correctness finding while reviewing technicals.ts: swingLevels() sorts its detected 45-session pivot highs/lows by raw MAGNITUDE (dedup() sorts ascending by value, then .slice(-5)/.slice(0,5) picks the top/bottom 5) rather than by distance to current spot. This means support_levels[0] is always the single LOWEST support pivot in the lookback window and resistance_levels[0] is always the single HIGHEST resistance pivot -- the FARTHEST level from price among everything detected, not the nearest. Both direct consumers read index [0] with no re-sort in between: deterministic-edition.ts's resolveLevels() (firstFinite(tech?.support_levels)/firstFinite(tech?.resistance_levels), lines 334-335 -- the CORE synthesis path for every deterministically-generated Legacy play) and play-backfill.ts's thin-edition rescue (dossier.tech?.support_levels?.[0]/resistance_levels?.[0], lines 132-133). Traced why this hasn't shown up as a target_unreachable/band_detached publish-gate failure: play-levels.ts's buildDirectionalStockLevels() clamps the resulting stop/target distance to a volatility-scaled max cap (and floors a too-close target, the documented PR-N21/N22 fix) on BOTH sides, so the final published number lands in a sensible ATR-scaled band regardless of whether the seed level was near or far -- an unrelated safety clamp absorbs the bug's numeric consequences. What doesn't get absorbed: when the farthest-pivot value happens to already sit inside that clamp band (common for a moderately volatile name), it's used as-is, so the play's stop/target is anchored to -- and any level-context text cites -- the LEAST relevant technical level available rather than the nearest one. A picks-quality/narrative-honesty issue, not a geometry-safety one, but it touches the core level-selection logic for every Legacy play. Confirmed zero test coverage of swingLevels()'s ordering semantics exists (technicals.test.ts only covers classifySetup/buildTechnicalSummary) -- this reads as an oversight, not a verified deliberate design choice. checkIns.codeReview: legacy-primary-pnl.ts (25 lines, marks-correctness relevant): legacyPrimaryPnlPct uses a bare `play.pnlPct ?? play.stockMovePct ?? null`, while its three siblings in the same file (legacyPrimaryPeakPct/legacyPrimaryTroughPct/legacyUsesOptionPnl) all explicitly guard with `Number.isFinite(play.pnlPct)` before trusting it. `??` only catches null/undefined, not NaN -- so IF play.pnlPct could ever be a NaN number (not null), legacyPrimaryPnlPct would return NaN instead of falling back to stockMovePct, while legacyUsesOptionPnl would correctly report false -- an internal contradiction between two functions describing the same play. Traced BOTH real producers of play.pnlPct in the Legacy pipeline to check reachability: (1) use-legacy-quotes.ts's overlayLegacyQuotes always sets pnlPct: null explicitly (its own fail-closed stock-vs-option-P&L guard, already reviewed this session); (2) use-legacy-option-marks.ts's overlayLegacyOptionMarks sets pnlPct via marks-math.ts's pinnedLivePnlPct(entryPrem, mark), which explicitly guards entryPremium<=0/null/mark==null and returns null rather than dividing -- entryPrem is separately validated >0 before the call and mark is validated Number.isFinite && >0 by the caller's own earlier guard. NEITHER producer can ever emit NaN -- play.pnlPct is always exactly null or a real finite number in this pipeline today. CONCLUSION: the `??` vs `Number.isFinite` inconsistency is a real code-style asymmetry but NOT a reachable bug given the current producers -- considered and dismissed, not escalated. Worth a defensive-coding note for whoever next adds a THIRD pnlPct producer to this pipeline (a raw division without the same guard would silently break legacyPrimaryPnlPct's fallback while legacyUsesOptionPnl stayed correct), but not actionable today.

checkIns.found: Real bug in the timeout-fallback machinery this route's own comments have already been incident-driven-fixed 3 times (#4599, #4961, 2026-09-14): lastGoodEdition (documented as 'this process's own last successful read', served when a 500ms maxBlockMs timeout fires) was only ever ASSIGNED on the cold-cache-miss branch (peekServerCache returns null). Traced server-cache.ts: peekServerCache serves a stale-while-revalidate hit for up to 10 minutes since last refresh, and the underlying store gets refreshed by withServerCache's own background mechanism roughly every 60s TTL window under traffic -- so once a replica serves one request past cold start, peekServerCache returns non-null on essentially every subsequent request for the rest of that replica's life. The fast path (if(instant)) fires a background refresh but discarded its resolved value with a bare .catch(()=>undefined). Net effect: lastGoodEdition froze at this process's FIRST successful resolve, not its LATEST -- a maxBlockMs timeout hours into a replica's life would replay a snapshot missing every pull/outcome overlay applied since boot, despite the variable's own doc comment promising otherwise.

knownOpenItems.legacyCalendarTileNullPremiumAsZero_2026:
Live finding, 2026-09-15 ~14:37 UTC: today's calendar day-tile (SEP 15) reads '+0%' even though VNCE (the day's only play) is up ~+10-12% stock move and near its target -- because VNCE is stock-only (no options data), its premiumPct is genuinely null (fail-closed, by design -- see use-legacy-quotes.ts's own MU-$880C comment), but legacyBoardCalendarBuckets (legacy-board-table-utils.ts:174-206) computes 'net = resolved.reduce((s,r) => s + (r.premiumPct ?? 0), 0)' then 'net_premium_pct: resolved.length ? Math.round(net / resolved.length) : 0' -- the ?? 0 coalesce means a null premiumPct (no data) is indistinguishable from an actually-measured 0% return in the divisor/numerator, so a day whose only play(s) are all stock-only silently reads as 'flat' rather than 'no premium data yet'. This is exactly the absence-read-as-presence trap this codebase's own audit discipline (LARGO-PRODUCT-CONTRACT.md's absence principle, the pulled-play net_premium fix already in this same function's comment) exists to prevent -- and it's a real, reproducible, current-day live instance, not a hypothetical. NOT shipped as a fix -- the clean fix (excluding null-premiumPct rows from the averaging denominator, and representing 'zero real data points' distinctly from 'measured zero') needs the bucket to carry a has_data flag or a nullable net_premium_pct, and VectorBoardCalendarBucket / fmtSigned (VectorBoardCalendar.tsx) are SHARED across other lanes' boards (0DTE/Swings also use vector-board-table-utils.ts's family of types) -- outside Legacy's ownership boundary per the standing mandate ('Not yours: 0DTE or Swings'). Flagging for operator/Cursor review rather than touching a shared type unilaterally. Candidate fix direction (not decided): legacyBoardCalendarBuckets could compute its own Legacy-local 'has real premium data' flag without changing the shared type's shape, if the render layer can be taught to treat a specific sentinel (e.g. n>0 but winners+closed+0-net all zero) as ambiguous -- needs a real design decision either way, not a mechanical patch.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-15 (new-hour :06 cycle): investigated the shared vector-board-row-utils.ts 'AVG GIVEBACK' stat (rendered as an honest '--' on today's board) as a fresh angle, and found strong reinforcing evidence for the recommended fix direction here. vectorBoardScorecard (SAME file) already computes netPremiumPct, hitRate, winnersFloorPct, runnerPipelinePct, AND avgGivebackPct ALL with the exact 'null when no real data, never a fabricated 0' pattern -- each uses its own counted-denominator variable (pctN/hitDenom/openTotal/givebackN) incremented only on real values, and returns `null` (not 0) when that counter is 0. So the eventual fix for legacyBoardCalendarBuckets's net_premium_pct (making it nullable, '--' in the UI for a genuinely-no-premium-data day) would not be a novel design choice -- it would be copying an already-dominant, four-times-repeated pattern in this exact file. This doesn't change the scope call (still a shared VectorBoardCalendarBucket type change, still outside Legacy's ownership boundary, still not shipped this session) but makes the case for whoever picks it up much stronger and lower-risk than a from-scratch design decision would be.

ADDENDUM 2 2026-09-15 (:36 cycle): took a fresh live desktop screenshot of /nighthawk?view=LEGACY now that VNCE has crossed target (currently +8% stock move, TARGET PATH 93%, green, status CONFIRMED). Hit rate 0%', WINNERS FLOOR shows 'Open winners 0%', RUNNER PIPELINE shows 'Open runners 0%' -- ALL despite VNCE being a real, currently-winning stock move 93% of the way to its target. NOT shipped. Flagging with this concrete live evidence (93%-to- target stock-only play reading 0% everywhere) so operator/Cursor have a vivid, reproducible case to reason about, not just an abstract description.
